units.source_text: 将我比作此花，实甚肖似，使我不禁堕泪。”

en.t: Comparing me to this flower is truly apt, and it makes me shed tears despite myself."

units.source_text: 书中仅此数语，并无何等深情。

en.t: The letter contained only these few words, with no especially deep feeling in them.

units.source_text: 但源氏内大臣不知何故，捧书细读，手不忍释。

en.t: Yet for some reason Minister Genji held the letter and read it closely, unable to bear putting it down.

units.source_text: 信纸青灰色，笔致柔嫩，非常美观。

en.t: The writing paper was bluish gray, and the brushwork was soft and delicate, extremely beautiful to look at.

units.source_text: 凡赠答之诗歌函牍，往往因人物之品格及笔墨之风趣得以遮丑，在当时似乎无甚缺陷；

en.t: In general, poems and letters exchanged as gifts often have their flaws concealed by the character of the people involved and the charm of the brushwork, so at the time they seem to have little wrong with them;

units.source_text: 但后来一经照样传抄，有的令人看了就要颦眉。

en.t: but once they are later copied down exactly as they were, some make readers frown as soon as they see them.

units.source_text: 因此作者自作聪明地引用在本书中的诗歌函牍，有伤大雅的想必甚多。

en.t: Therefore, among the poems and letters that the author cleverly chose to quote in this book, there must be many that offend refined taste.
